text:
incident-bot: PAGER - ALERT TRIGGERED: gpu-node-eviction-rate spike · service=runtime-usw2 · severity=P2 · paged oncall
incident-bot: summary: 18 node evictions in last 3m, increased VRAM reclamation, thermals trending up on rack-7, some pods recycled. auto-escalation window started.

sam: ack — I’m on it. picking up context.

maya: pulling dashboards now. looking at node metrics: GPU memory used ~82% avg but per-process VRAM spikes to 97% on a few nodes. PCIe errors normal, but ECC count jumped on node-gpu-07.

alisha: reassigning traffic away from rack-7 briefly. starting node drains for nodes with >5 evictions.

maya: quick note — embeddings API 5xxs spike correlated with these draining nodes. CS reported customers seeing ~1.8% error rate during the window. lia, can you confirm impact?

lia: yup CS confirms two customers saw increased latencies and a few retries, nothing persisted to storage. they flagged an SLA blip, but are not escalating yet. sharing logs. :grimacing:

sam: mitigation plan: 1) drain noisy nodes 2) scale dedicated pool by +2 nodes (hot spare) 3) temporarily raise eviction sensitivity so transient VRAM bursts don't evict as aggressively.

alisha: draining node-gpu-05 and node-gpu-07 now:
```
kubectl drain node-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl cordon node-gpu-05
```

deploy-bot: action: scale runtime-dedicated-pool replicas from 12 -> 14 requested by alisha. CI job queued.

maya: digging into metrics — looks like a nightly batch (model embedding compaction) started at 02:12 and caused simultaneous KV cache reloads on several pods. causing momentary VRAM pressure.

sam: ok that explains the correlation with the 02:10 scheduled job. did we have a node-affinity for the batch that concentrated it on rack-7?

maya: yes, affinity changed in last week’s rollout; batch shard pinned to nodes that live on rack-7 to reduce cross-rack traffic. that increased local VRAM contention.

greg: recommendation for immediate alert tuning: change alert gpu_vram_utilization_high from threshold 80% sustained 2m -> 90% sustained 5m for the dedicated pool, and add an annotation to ignore scheduled batch windows (02:00-03:00). will open a PR to alerts repo.

sam: agree on temp change. but we should be careful — we still want real degradation to page. set a separate alert for eviction-rate > 5/min that remains P2.

maya: creating dashboard snippet for on-call: added panel for per-node "evictions/min", "vrm_peak_per_process", and ECC_errors. saving to /dashboards/runtime/gpu-health/nightshift.

alisha: drains completed, scaled pool +2 done (deploy-bot shows success). traffic shifted, 5xxs dropping back to baseline.

lia: CS updated customers, they want a postmortem if this repeats. asking for ETA on a fix.

sam: short-term actions (this thread):
- greg: PR for alert threshold change + ignore window (owner: greg)
- maya: revert affinity change for batch sharding or spread shards across racks (owner: maya)
- alisha: bake a canary that runs the compaction on spare nodes to validate load (owner: alisha)
- sam: write short incident note and customer impact summary (owner: sam)

greg: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/monitoring/pull/482
PR diff includes:
```yaml
- alert: GPUVRAMHigh
- expr: avg_over_time(gpu_vram_utilization[2m]) > 0.80
+ alert: GPUVRAMHigh
+ expr: avg_over_time(gpu_vram_utilization[5m]) > 0.90 unless on_batch_window
```

maya: small query to identify affected nodes:
```promql
sum by (node) (increase(gpu_evictions_total[5m])) > 0
```
saved as runtime_gpu/evictions_by_node-nightshift

sam: handoff plan — I need to go offline in ~25m. lia, can you coordinate CS messaging if anything else happens? I’ll leave the thread.

lia: yep I’ll watch and ping if customers start re-escalating.

alisha: follow-up — we should build a dashboard alert suppressor that detects scheduled batch windows and auto-suppresses VRAM noise alerts for that window but keeps eviction-rate alerts active. filing ticket.

incident-bot: NOTE: auto-escalation suppressed after manual mitigation. incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

sam: post-incident notes for runbook: add explicit guidance to avoid pinning memory-heavy scheduled jobs to single racks; add gating in deploy pipeline to warn on node-affinity configs that reduce rack spread.

greg: also adding an alert annotation for "potential-scheduled-batch" when we see VRAM spikes exactly on 02:00-03:00 to reduce paging fatigue.

alisha: created ticket INFRA-2198: implement alert suppressor + affinity-lint in deploy.

sam: last ask — can someone spin up a quick dashboard for customer-impact metrics (5xx rate, p99 latency for embeddings) tied to node drain events? we want faster triage next time.

maya: on it, will add a panel and link in the runbook.

deploy-bot: scale job completed at 1933007810.

sam: thanks all — good catch. going to write up short incident summary and schedule a 30m review tomorrow morning. please leave any follow ups here. :thumbsup:
